summary.headline: JK Lakshmi Q1 FY27: realisation up ~8-9% QoQ on geo-mix and non-trade price gains, but management guides to a sharp Q2 cost squeeze from fuel and packaging.
summary.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 demand was reasonable, with industry growth around 8%, and the company's realisation rose roughly 9% sequentially, driven mainly by a 20 km reduction in lead distance (to 368 km from 388 km) and higher non-trade prices in Gujarat, Mumbai, East and North. Fuel cost per Kcal rose to INR1.65 from INR1.54 in Q4, and management expects Q2 fuel cost of 1.8-1.85 plus packaging inflation of INR3.5-4 per bag, with July-September demand cyclicality compounding the pressure. Management reiterated 30 MTPA by FY30 and a net debt/EBITDA ceiling of 2.5x, stretching to 2.75x at peak. Management also described the proxy-advisor-driven AGM voting outcome and an Assam PIL affecting the Northeast project.

financial_highlights.value: INR185 crore (RMC INR93 cr, AAC INR60 cr, POP INR23 cr)

financial_highlights.change: Trade share rose to 59% from prior level

segments.name: Cement (core)
segments.commentary: Realisation rose ~9% QoQ, helped by non-trade price increases in Gujarat, Mumbai, East and North and a 20 km lead reduction worth about INR60-70/tonne. Roughly 90% of sales came from Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Haryana and western UP.

segments.name: Non-cement (RMC, AAC, POP)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR185 crore in Q1 with 5% EBITDA margin. Management expects FY27 non-cement revenue near INR800 crore vs INR613 crore last year.

segments.name: Renewable energy / power
segments.commentary: 49% of power from renewables. Installed: solar 129 MW, WHRS 45 MW, wind 4 MW, thermal 74 MW. A 42 MW solar captive SPV (INR20 crore investment) at INR4.10 tariff against grid INR7.50 is expected to be live in 8-9 months.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 fuel cost per Kcal expected to rise from INR1.65 to about INR1.8-1.85, with management saying the cost impact is larger than Q1.
Packaging granule cost up, adding about INR3.5-4 per bag versus Q1 as per initial calculation.
Management expects some pass-through of cost, but says the extent is uncertain given July-September demand cyclicality and maintenance.
Installed/operational capacity targeted at 18 MTPA by end FY27; 30 MTPA by FY30 reiterated.

FY27 capex about INR1,500 crore, FY28 about INR2,000 crore, FY29 about INR1,500 crore (including Northeast; excluding Kutch and Nagaur land acquisition). Durg has about INR400 crore spent to date out of about INR3,000 crore.
Lead distance expected to rise during monsoon/lean months (July-September) but management aims to contain it.
capex_capacity: Durg expansion: about INR400 crore spent to date, INR300 crore in Q1; equipment ordering for Durg clinker and grinding, plus Prayagraj and Madhubani grinding, largely complete.

Northeast: two mines won via auction at various approval stages; initial 1.5 MTPA planned with grinding station sites still being identified; management says project is back on track with milestone updates next quarter.
Overhead conveyor belt approval from SAIL is granted and agreement is with SAIL for execution; railway siding phase 2 is contingent on SAIL and state road collaboration.
Assam PIL filed in Guwahati High Court involving land for the Mahabal Cement (subsidiary) grinding plant; JK Lakshmi has been named as a recipient of the notice.
BESS of 28 MW planned as part of Rajasthan solar setup to store excess captive generation.
demand_pricing: Industry demand grew ~8% in Q1; industry capacity added about 11 MT in the quarter, about 52 MT expected for the year, taking national capacity to about 725 MT; industry utilisation about 73-74%.
Non-trade prices rose in several markets; trade was flat in North, up in West and East; trade prices in July and early August have not fallen and have seen little upward movement.
Management believes North has pricing headroom because it was most impacted by imported coal/pet coke costs; East/Chhattisgarh prices are seen as lowest in India with room to rise.
Management said trade is the focus going forward because blended cement sells in trade and offers better equivalent realisation, though non-trade margins can be higher in absolute terms.
Far-off markets were reduced in Q1 to concentrate on core states; management says demand months are used to expand channel reach and lean months to spread wider.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ~9% sequential realisation increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited non-trade price increases in Gujarat, Mumbai, East and North, trade gains in West and East, and a 20 km lead reduction worth about INR60-70/tonne; the rest was price and geo-mix. Non-trade is 41% of volume.

qa_highlights.question: Fuel cost trajectory into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 fuel cost INR1.65/Kcal vs INR1.54 in Q4. Q2 is expected to exceed 1.65, potentially reaching 1.8-1.85. Imported coal is about USD130-135/t and pet coke has risen above USD140-145/t.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 margin outlook given cost increases and cyclical demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full pass-through is uncertain due to July-September seasonal weakness and maintenance; it expects to pass costs on but cannot quantify how much.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan and whether Northeast is included?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 about INR1,500 crore, FY28 about INR2,000 crore, FY29 about INR1,500 crore; this includes Northeast (INR1,500 crore) and Durg (about INR3,000 crore total); Kutch and Nagaur land is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Leverage ceiling and the 30 MTPA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not cross 2.5x net debt/EBITDA, and at most 2.75x near the end of the expansion plan; 30 MTPA by 2030 is reaffirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material cost inflation QoQ and YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Cited kiln shutdowns requiring fly ash from L2 sources at higher cost, gypsum availability, diesel, and higher SBS/non-cement raw material use. Trade share rising to 59% and blended share rising also drove cementitious material cost.
